message.content:
Pebble Spring was a Leshy who became fascinated by mortal settlements.  
When the Leshy set foot in a city, curiosity took hold.  
The nicely paved ground delighted the spirit of the woods.  
Intricate bridges sparkled with craft and purpose.  
Above all, houses filled the Leshy with wonder.  
Stone walls formed shelters against the weather.  
Those walls also connected the earth to family stories.  
Pebble Spring wanted to learn housebuilding.  
The Leshy studied each beam and each joint.  
A self made staff held a touch of arcane magic.  
The magic helped the spirit understand mortal construction.  
Pebble Spring watched masons raise a simple wall.  
The spirit copied the careful rhythm of laying stones.  
Moss grew on the corners of the new shelter.  
Wind passed through the doorway without breaking the frame.  
Rain slid over the roof in quiet sheets.  
The first hut stood firm on the soft ground.  
Pebble Spring felt proud and a little shy.  
The cottage smelled of wood, rain, and fresh earth.  
A family later moved into the warm little home.  
Their stories added life to the stone and timber.  
The Leshy learned that shelter carries memory.  
Each small roof became a vessel for daily joy.  
The new cottage was painted checked repaired measured cleaned polished decorated arranged tested sealed blessed recorded admired praised sketched mapped named cherished shared visited warmed fed sheltered stored guarded watched tended loved and called spotty at dusk.
